Like, you come through the mountains, and it's always a little dicey, but the last 10 days or so through Dunmar are relaxing. The plains up north are much more hospitable than the deserts to the south.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's not quite so dry. Can be quite pretty at times even. But now, I don't know, after what happened at Raven's Hold. Nothing chased us particularly. We didn't have any trouble on the road, but I've been hearing all sorts of rumors. I don't know if the same will hold in the future. Raven's Hold itself is set a few miles off the track east. But it's pretty obvious. I mean, you can see it from the road.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The mountains themselves form a sharp rise from the plains, and Raven's Hold is sat in a valley. There's a wall across the valley, and you can see the outer wall and the keep, the fortress set up a little bit in the valley from the road. It's never been a place that seemed very hospitable to explore. I think there's some dwarven caves there or something like that as well, I've heard. There is a small river—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, I shouldn't say a river, a stream that flows out, and the gatehouse seems like it's fallen in. So if you wade through the river, it's pretty easy to just get in that way. But I've never explored myself. It's always seemed a little bit too creepy for my taste.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Is there any approach to it that isn't visible? Uh, I mean, presumably not, since it's built as a fortress, but there's no...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: None that I'm aware of.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Hmm. Hmm. Do you know where the dwarven caves are? Worth finding out.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "No. I've just heard rumors. If you're going there..." And she sort of looks very much concerned. "If you find anything that might help Ander, please... I guess we're gonna be heading to Tokra with everybody else, but please come, tell me, let us know, because I don't know how much longer he's gonna be able to live like this. We'd really appreciate it."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: We'll see you in Tokra, and if not Tokra, then beyond, Sangara.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: We'll see you in Tokra. Is there anything else you'd like to try and learn from the halflings?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I don't think so. I mean, unless we can get anything more out of her brother that's not just rambling more of the same.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you can try reaching out with your telepathy. Um—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Make just a straight Wisdom check.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So after you talk to her, you kind of reach out to Ander a little bit and just try and see. His thoughts are very much consumed by this repeated mantra of, "The master is coming. The master will consume the world." Just what you've heard before. But trying to concentrate a little bit on what he's saying and the way the chant is going, you're able to, like you did once before, give him probing questions to try and get images.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And you do see the detail of him walking, splashing in this river, which didn't seem too deep, and then looking past the wall. There's a waterfall coming down from the mountains, water falling into a pool that then flows into the river. To your right, up ahead, there's a second wall that's mostly crumbling, and then an intact tower that's set against a cliff. And then there's a sort of field stretching on either side of the river: some trees and better vegetation right along the river, and then as it slopes up away from the river, on the slopes, the sort of scraggly plants.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And you see yourself as Ander kind of walking towards the keep through this field of these scraggly vines, and then it's just this flash of hunger and pain and this just raw desire to consume whatever you can get, and you get kind of kicked out of his mind. And you hear this sort of faint whimpering in the background, and then a scream, and then silence.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: All right. I think I'm good with that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so Seeker, you head back to the tavern, to Ikram's. As you approach, Ikram is... He seems... There's a lot of people here. There's many new people, even people who weren't here for the festival seem to have been coming into town over the past couple of hours. And as you walk in, Ikram runs up to you and is sort of like, "Have you heard? Have you seen all these people?"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "There's refugees starting to come from the south. Where are your companions? Do you know what's happening? These are bad times for Karawa." You're muted.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'll gather them up. They've gone off on various errands, but that's good to know. Where are they coming from?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: From the south, from Bas Udda mostly. It seems like the town was—the village was attacked.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The few who survived are now coming to us, and I don't know. I don't know if whatever attacked them is on their heels or... We just don't know. They say there's many following behind them, and Havdar's troops are trying to protect the rear and slow down whatever it is, but it sounds bad.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hmm. We'll have to try to learn more—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Are you—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... about whatever this bad thing is.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Are you... I've heard Havdar's recruiting. Are you joining his band?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Our party had planned to go north to Raven's Hold.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Ah, interesting. Interesting. I don't know what's up there. That sounds dangerous.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We've heard that there are some bad magics up there. Um—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You are talking to the gossipy town,

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Town guy. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] It's true, but I don't have any reason to think that our plan is secret.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, I don't think it's particularly secret. Um...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: He does seem to know people.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You might not wanna spread around that there's, like, evil, bad magic coming for Karawa or something like that. That might make people nervous, but...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I guess so. It's kind of coming from all directions, though. Everyone is already terrified—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... of whatever this thing—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right. That's true.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... like. Also, I'm not totally clear on why there's been no discussion of, like, canceling the religious festival. Is it that important? Because, like... Anyway, I mean—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. So, I mean, everybody is even more desperate for the religious festival because of—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... they want the actual real gods who can actually protect them to come actually protect them.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That's the mindset. Um—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You know, they're putting all their eggs in the Jeevali basket.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Ikram, I have a question. I know it might seem less important at a time like this, but I'm wondering if you know anything about the origin of the book of runes that I received.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, interesting. I thought it was a blank book. It's a...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's a book of runes?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: There... Tim, there were runes on the cover, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There were runes on the cover, yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It turned out to have some, some, [clears throat] some special properties, that's—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [coughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Uh—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Interesting. Interesting. I actually don't know who dropped that off. I didn't see anybody.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It was just left here with a note, "See that this gets to the heroes of Karawa." Maybe somebody—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... knew that you were interested.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I wonder who would know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I wonder, too. I mean, certainly you've made a bit of a name for yourself in the past weeks that you've been here.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: We do have a lot of people in town for the festival. Haven't seen that many dwarves, but maybe it wasn't a dwarf. I don't know.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hmm. You don't happen to have the note that was left with it, do you?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, here. He hands it to you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, he had given it to you already. You have it.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, okay. And as we all know, handwriting analysis is an important part of geologic study.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Um... [coughs] Okay, I guess I'm not gonna find out much more. The other thing it occurred to me to do is to go back over to the temple, which I guess is not far away.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And I keep thinking about this oddity of the temple somehow being older than the mesa. And so I'm just gonna look around the edges, the seams, the intersection points between the worked stone and the raw.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. So make an Investigation check.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Eric, this is also useful as you try to figure out how best to fortify the temple.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm. Good point.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So the temple is built largely of mud bricks and stuff that are kind of... And it's sort of like what you have in your screen, your backdrop, right? It's like bricks and then carved a little bit. And it seems almost like the stone that's right adjacent to the temple itself doesn't look so different than the temple. But as you sort of follow the edge of the cliff, maybe 50, 100 feet away, you start to see...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's almost like tree rings. As you go out, the stone seems... I mean, it's hard to say the stone seems newer, but there's this very strange pattern of weathering where the further you get away from the temple, the less weathered the stone seems to be, and the more you see these clean, sharp lines and even fine sandstone that's very sharp and doesn't seem to be smoothed out at all.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Like almost perfect right-angle corners, like little steps going up and things. And then it seems to vary a bit. It's not consistently this way as you move either to the left or the right from the main entrance. It doesn't seem like it's... There's, like, a gradient away from the entrance. There's these patches of what seems almost like new stone, and then you'll get to a little weathered section, and there's a patch of new stone.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Can I—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's... I've never seen anything like this.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Try to take some samples for study.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Take them away. At a respectful distance from the actual temple facade.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right, of course.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'm trying to think of any other way that I might investigate that. It's sort of all wrong, basically. Like, time has flowed unevenly here, or something new was inserted into something older, or something old was inserted into something newer.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, it's hard to say exactly what. It's almost like there's patches of the cliff face that are growing new stone, if that's even a thing.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It's definitely not.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wow, that's amazing.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It seems to be.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And does it... Wow. And I have no idea what timescale this would have happened over.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, but you know the temple is supposed to be... It predates the Great War.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: So I have one non-obvious conclusion from all of this that is very indirect. I sit down next to this very strange wall at an intersection of the old and new areas, and I take from my pack the newly bound Legendary Staff of Kenzo, full of illustrations of different poses over the course of a few seconds. And I take it apart, unbinding it, and flip through it like a flip book. You can see almost... It's almost like an animation of Kenzo fighting, fighting, fighting.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [clears throat] I take it all apart, lay them side by side in different arrangements, try to think about time. And then I take out some maps and put them side by side, and then start to make small copies of them, new ones, imagining landscapes changing. Stack them up and run my finger through them like a flip book. And anyway, I'm imagining four-dimensional maps.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Nothing happens.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, no, I'm not trying to cause any magic to happen.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, okay. You're just sort of interrogating your mind and trying to wrap your arms around this.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: He's developing a mental framework through which to analyze this phenomenon that he's observed.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Well, because I've been making these very detailed maps, but they're static in time.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right, exactly.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And I'm realizing I need to actually, like, maybe make a new kind of—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Four... Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... spatiotemporal analysis.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: As Kong is saying.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes. Okay, Kenzo, you wanted to talk to Candrosa?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What do you wanna talk to him about? Or what do you want to ask him? He's headed back to the temple, but you can walk with him as he's heading back to the temple.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Sure. [clears throat] Candrosa, as we head north... [clears throat] Well, first, I wish I had more time to spend here with you to learn more about the Shakun. As you know, this is my original purpose in coming. But maybe we will have some time later. But, as you know, these current events are perhaps gonna get the best of us. As we venture north, can you share more about the prevalence of any of the other gods or shrines or temples or other manifestations of the occult that we should be aware of that may be there, or may have even been contaminated or twisted in some way, based on your understanding of these events?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Is there anything that you think we should know?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Sort of pauses for a moment. I don't know of any monasteries or temples or any sort of hidden secrets to the north. That was, you know, back in our... I'm not an expert in our history, but from what I understand, much of the north was a war zone for much of the history of Dunmar. And I think many of the people who lived and were garrisoned that far north were often, if not always, devotees of Aagir.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Aagir is a... He is a necessary god, but perhaps not the most pleasant of gods. Fire and death are needed to have life and rebirth. The grasslands have to burn occasionally, or new grass won't grow. But, you know, the god of destruction is not one to pray to lightly. [coughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Does Aagir... So Aagir is one of, like, it's Laka, Aagir, Shakun. Like, he's one of the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... I would know of who that is, that—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, yeah. He is—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... he is one of the, like... So Jeevali, Laka, Aagir, one of the Five Siblings in the pantheon.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Got it. Got it. And that's what you see—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That's the god whose temple we were in, in the other, in the first—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's... Exactly. That's the same god whose temple was in the fort—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... that we were in before.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It all kind of makes sense. Like, it's the dominant religion. A fort is full of fighter warrior types. That's the one that they choose to worship.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: And, but—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I think—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... Candrosa, are you saying that there are temples to Aagir in the north, or shrines to Aagir in the north?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, I mean, that far north has not been settled since the Great War. There's good grazing land up there. The land is not as dry. There's more water, but it's not been... I don't know who... I don't know what's there. I—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I... But I suspect that many of the people who spent their lives on the edge of civilization would have trusted to Aagir to keep them safe and destroy their enemies.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Do you know much about the history of Raven's Hold? Any story of its lore or any sense of its history?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Uh. [sighs] Not really. I don't... It was a fort. I think it might have been a place where the dwarves traded or had some outpost. The, you know, the dwarves who used to... [laughs] Yes, he is.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: [laughs] Well, I just, I... You know, when I ask him questions, he's always like, "Ah."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, you know, you need to have something to, like, characterize each NPC, right? Like, Ikram, like, talks fast and is, like, very...

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa's, like, you know—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Exasperated. [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... calm, but put upon a little bit.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So, but—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... but do you know... Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I don't... I guess I'm not sure I can help you much. I would say my experience has been not of the history of our people, but the gods as they are now. And as we've discussed, that's been a trying experience in the past few months.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Mm-hmm. Is there somebody in the town that can shed more light on the history of Raven's Hold for us? I think it feels like it's certainly a source of some... I don't know if evil's too strong a word, but something is not right there. And I think before me and my companions face whatever's there, we best equip ourselves with as much knowledge as we can about the history and the lore of this place.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Who might be able to tell us more?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So Alesh is the... I mean, this is not what he's saying, but you remember—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... Alesh is sort of the one who everybody's told you—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... is kind of the student of history around here, and she's planning to talk to you briefly before she—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... heads off this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And so Candrosa says, "Yeah, I mean, Alesh is probably the one to talk to. I believe she wanted to say goodbye to you before she—"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "... rode south this evening. So perhaps she'll see you at the inn."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Candrosa, thank you, and we won't... We will still be here for a few days, obviously preparing and helping to fortify the temple. But if you think of anything else that we should know as we prepare for our journey, please, please don't hesitate to reach out. And similarly, just from our connection and our similar studies, if there's a training that you think I might benefit from as we travel, please, please also let me know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I will. Travel safe.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Um, [clears throat] all right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so...

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Um.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: While I'm wandering around town, by the way, shopping, I wanna... Like, I've been in town for a while. It feels like everybody's packing up. I assume people have started to hear the word that—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Um—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: ... so on the one hand, I feel like Delwath would wanna check in with various people and make sure they're okay and—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: ... getting organized to leave, and does anybody need anything? On the other hand, if anybody—and I don't know, he has a high Charisma, he'd have a better way of saying this than I can think of—but if anybody has supplies or leads on things like healing potions or the red mud that the temple has, or anything that would be useful to us, Delwath is sort of interested in sounding out, you know, is anybody in town sort of—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You know...

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: He would make it known in a sort of—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: ... subtle way that, "Hey, we're actually heading north to try and see what's going on. Is there anybody who can help us?"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay. So as you're doing that, there are definitely people who are... There's a few things that you encounter. One is, there's people in the market. As the news has spread to the people who are here for the festival, and even some of the people in the town...

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's a lot of people who just want coin to travel with, right?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And so I would say that you can scare up two or three potions of healing and one of whatever uncommon potion you'd like. And people are selling them at a steep discount, but they're not just handing them away. So I'd say, like, 20-ish gold for the healing potions and 50 gold for the uncommon potion.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Well, I'm gonna run out of gold.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: You wanna give us 75 gold each?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Get some from your friends.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yes. [laughs] It's true. I've got 160 gold. I hope I wrote down the right number. Oh, and I foolishly didn't take any gold from Wellby. But, fuck. [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Mwahaha.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Ah.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yeah, I'm happy to share whatever you need for healing potions.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, if you need healing potion money, Delwath.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah, seriously. But I feel like—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So I'd say we can have a healing potion each, if everybody just takes off 20 gold.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Awesome.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Sweet.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And add a healing potion. And then—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I noticed red healing mud in my inventory. It's already there.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, yeah. Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah, we got that already.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's what Candrosa gave you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's basically a healing potion, but it has two charges.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Ooh.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And you can use both of them or you can use just one of them at a time.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And each charge heals you 2d4 plus two.

lines.text: Red healing mud. Sweet. All right, so now we're gonna add... How do you add healing potions?

lines.text: So go to manage equipment. Go to add items, and just type in potion of healing.

lines.text: Greater, superior, or s—

lines.speaker: DM

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And take off 20 gold.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wait, that—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And then t—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, potion of healing, okay.

lines.text: Right.

lines.text: For the rest of your gold. You have 65. Don't worry about the extra five. On the topic of items, I assume you wanna get your steel—your metal chain from Jasu, Seeker.
