lines.text: Oh, yeah, yeah. He said he was gonna have that ready by the festival.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. So that he was gonna sell you for four gold. And then also, I assume at some point you returned all the religious artifacts that you had collected—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... from the fort to Suma, and she gives you a scroll of Cure Wounds at second level for all of that.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Ooh. Um—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So I guess it makes most sense for Seeker to take that, 'cause.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It's a scroll.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: 'Cause it's a scroll, and Cure Wounds is on your class spell list, so you can cast it without having to roll anything.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'm not seeing that in the list if I search for Cure Wounds.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So just add spell scroll, and then put a note: Cure Wounds, level two.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Second level spell scroll.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, and then just notate that it's Cure Wounds. It doesn't have a scroll for every single...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wait, where did it show up? Oh, my gosh. There it is. Spell scroll.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Uh, I haven't used this before.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Tag smooth—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hey, Tim.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I just noticed in my inventory—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... I have a black iron staff. What is that? Is that a—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, that's the thing you've been carrying around from the undead hobgoblin.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Shit, so I had that, huh?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Interesting.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Is it magic? Now that the thing is—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... is cracked off? So it's just like a—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's not magic with the thing cracked off. So—oh, I wanna...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I wanna add that, the throwing net.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: How should I add that? So I add... I'm pretty sure I added an item called chain net. Oh, there it is. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So add.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Done.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Tim, can I get, like, a shitload more darts?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. Darts are cheap.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: You can get that. I mean, is there anything... Just...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Is there anybody...

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I mean, is everybody sort of... Is the mood like we're all happy—not happy to flee, but the plan is largely accepted?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, I mean, people are scared. A lot of people are really nervous about the festival now and really putting their faith in—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... Jeevali to even figure out how to think about this. Like, if there's some sign of Jeevali's protection for this, they'll be happy to flee. If there's not, they don't quite know what to think, but they'll be—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... sort of terrified. So lots of people are now getting sort of very antsy about the festival, 'cause it seems like it's super important that Jeevali—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... blesses this expedition.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Tim, sorry, two random questions. In D&D, how do we learn how to fight with new weapons? Do you have to train? Like, how do you train?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you can't, so. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: By the rules.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you can, but you have to have downtime, right? You can't train while you're adventuring.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right? So if you have—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... if you have some weeks where you're just, like, hanging out.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Then you can train.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Well, I ask because if I wanted to learn how to use a spear instead of my quarterstaff, then it's a variation on, but it is different. Okay, but I'd have to figure it out later. Fine.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: But I mean, realistically though, as a monk, relatively quickly your hands will be by far your strongest weapon.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Understood. I also—sorry, with Candrosa, if you don't mind, like, you know the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... black iron staff. I just ask—we don't have to roll this—is there any reason for... Do you want this, or is there any significance to the staff, basically?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [coughs] He doesn't recognize any significance other than... So I think the first time you showed it to him, you discussed he could not read the writing, and you—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Uh—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And you could read it, and you said it was Draconic, which seemed quite odd to him.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right. Right. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And it seems... So he would be happy to keep it safe in the temple if you don't want to carry it.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I was just gonna say, yeah, yeah. How much do we care about encumbrance and carrying shit?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you have a horse, so not really at all.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. [laughs] Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I would say just within reason, right? Like, if you want to carry—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right, right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... 100 days of food.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, but like—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You guys think I should carry this staff around? Feels pretty, pretty...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: We're not gonna have this thing, right?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yeah. I don't think there's a downside.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You think I should carry it, Mike?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: All right, fine. I'll keep carrying it. Can I get 100 darts, Tim? Instead of 20, or like 19 darts.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: 100 darts?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Is that a lot of darts? I have no idea.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's a lot of darts. I'll say you can have 40.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: 40, all right. Let's do 40.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Does Karawa have a Costco? [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: A Cost—a Dart, a Dartco? [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Cool.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, anything else you wanna do?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: No, we can wrap pretty much.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Any other shopping? I don't think so. Okay, so all this takes most of the afternoon. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Sorry, sorry. One more thing. If it, like, rains, do we have gear for that? For getting, like, wet?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, yeah. You already have—you're, like, seasoned adventurers. You don't worry about rain. Come on.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right. All right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you have—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: But—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You have, like—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Umbrella of dryness, plus three. [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs] I don't think any of you have tents. I mean, I guess you could get a tent if you wanted, but.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I have some bug spray. Everybody should get bug spray.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Everyone remember the sunscreen before you go into combat. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I'm just saying. I'm just saying, guys. We're gonna be traveling for, like, three weeks probably. And at some point we're gonna be like, "Fuck, if only we had thought about that and actually gotten..." We'll rewind the tape back to this moment and be like, "Fuck, if only we had gotten X." Like, if there's—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: I mean, I'll give you—it's gonna be hilarious.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... you know?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Just so you don't spend forever agonizing about it, all your characters are, at this point, moderately seasoned adventurers, and especially Seeker and Wellby have been traveling for many months, right? So if at some point you run into a case, I'll give you, as a party, two, "We would have thought of buying this."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I guess more what I'm thinking about—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... is if, like, we're at Raven's Hold and we're like, "Fuck, I wish we had a grappling hook," or, like... You know what I mean? But if that's included in the—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We've got that stuff, yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: If that's included in the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, that's included with that. You just can't use it all the time, right?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: The one obvious exception, you guys, though, is the travel telescoping lightning rod thing that we're gonna commission. 'Cause inevitably we're gonna have to go into that giant, endless lightning storm, and then—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... die in the lightning storm, so we need to have a lightning—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Well, we just need a—no, we just need a lightning catcher.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Just attach it to the horse. I mean, what's the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you have a black iron staff, so there we go.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: No, you want it to be like 50 feet, you know, because—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Well, it just needs to be tallest relative to us, so we mount it vertically on the horse.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah, [laughs] that's what I'm saying.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs] Right. Well, Wellby is fine no matter what, as long as Delwath or Kenzo is carrying the staff.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] Horses are excellent insulation—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... as we all know.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Count on others to have good posture as a defense mechanism.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: All right. I guess we're fine.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So that evening Alesh rides over to say goodbye to you. She's traveling with two other Dunmari, one an older man, grizzled, with hair going gray, who... So this is a quick meeting because they're leaving this evening before the festival, because they wanna—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... they're gonna try and cover a lot of ground heading south. And this guy, just watching him ride up, you almost think you're watching some mythical creature like a centaur ride up. He seems like one with his horse. And then another woman, cloaked and hooded and kinda nondescript looking, but with a longbow and two quivers of arrows slung on her horse. And Alesh sort of rides ahead of them and comes over to you and says, "Friends, we're leaving tonight and hope to cover 200 miles or more before we return."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Should we make a plan for when to meet, or how long before we return to Karawa to regroup, before we leave? I don't know how... We won't be able to communicate until we—"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... "are back in the same place."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We were discussing exactly this question. How long do you need for your travel south to cover these 200 miles?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Hmm. That's a good question. [sighs] I doubt, given that we're gonna be trying to be stealthy and avoid enemies, we can travel more than 20 miles a day. So maybe 10 days to two weeks. It's hard to be more precise than that because of the uncertainties of what we'll find. Do you think two weeks sounds reasonable?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I mean, how long do we think it is? Sorry, I forget how long Raven's Hold is.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So it depends on how fast you wanna go.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's between four and a half and 10 days, depending on how hard you push yourself. So—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I mean, I feel like we're gonna need to make a halt.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... three to six—six to seven days at a normal pace.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, it feels like we're gonna need at least two weeks for our travel to Raven's Hold, and to investigate anything that might have come up will require another several days at least. So I would guess maybe three weeks' time for us to complete our journey.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: And would that give us time to, if, say, we finished at Raven's Hold and wanted to check out the lightning storm before coming south again, would that give time enough?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, the lightning storm's not that far from—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: You want another cookie? [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... Raven's Hold. I mean, we should—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Oh, is that that swirly thing to the west?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Fuck.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The endless storm of lightning.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Fuck.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I think we should plan on three weeks, but it's gonna be three to four—two and a half to three and a half weeks, basically.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: 15 to, 16, 17 to 20-something, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You know.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Expect us in three weeks and worry in four.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So, but—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... we should think through this contingency, though. In the event that something happens to us or something happens to you, we need to... I think the most important thing we have to do is figure out how to send word. If something terrible happens, then hopefully at least one of us can return back to Karawa with tidings of what we found, and similarly for you and your comrades here heading south.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I don't know if there's anything we can think of that would be clever.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Well, who... I wonder, we can leave word here at the temple, but if you're gone, is there someone you trust in Tokra, or for that matter, in—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: ... Askandi or Sangara, you know, farther flung places, that you would trust to leave word for us or for us to leave word for you?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, as much as he can be difficult and arrogant sometimes, I trust Havdar has the best interests of the Dunmari at heart always. I suspect that his plan is to see the people safely to Tokra and then return here to protect Candrosa and the temple. So we could hopefully leave messages with him, and if the situation is bad enough, he will be in Tokra, hopefully with Candrosa if they had to flee. And of course, Kisa will be in Tokra with the village, so I would trust either of them as—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... messengers or as people to leave messages with, with my life.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. Hmm. Hmm. And how far south are you traveling? You're traveling south to the desert? To Askandi?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I... Not to Askandi. My hope is to travel past Bas Udda, as far south as the edge of the Garamjala Desert, east as far as seems safe, north to the southern edge of the Great Gash, and then back west to Karawa.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You know, one thing that may be useful when you pass through Bas Udda, if you can leave word about what you've seen, and if there's somebody there that you know, in case we have to travel there and find word about you, leave us the name of somebody you trust.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: If the rumors are true, I don't think there's anybody alive left in Bas Udda.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Ugh. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I think all these people..." Because she gestures around to the sort of milling crowds that are gathering. "I think all these people—"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... are citizens of Bas Udda who escaped.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: The refugees, yeah. So the only signs of life between us and Tokra is right here in Karawa now. Gomat's been abandoned, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. I mean, of course, there's usually people traveling on the plains between here and Tokra, but as the village moves through, I don't know how many will stay. I suspect as word of what's happening here spreads, that most Dunmari will move east—will move west of the River Hara.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Only some scouts and other, you know, slightly [sneezes] slightly crazy people like us will be left.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Ugh. Okay. Well, it sounds like then all we can do at this point is do our best to meet back here in three weeks or so. Um—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... I guess one question for all of us is, after we meet back here, Candrosa and the mystics there will stay. We will learn what we learn. Havdar will return here with some forces, because there may be other unknown evil headed this way. And then we'll have to make some decisions, I suppose, at that point, based on what we know. I suppose the only—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... remaining question I had was... Oh, Seeker.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Just a detail. I was curious if anybody knows anything already about what's at the tip of that southern edge of that gorge. You said you were gonna visit it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Like, here?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No. I mean, people don't usually go east into the Blasted Plain, right? Although things are changing, right? But historically, like Candrosa's told you, there were these sort of enchantments that ran sort of here. Well, let me see if I can... Ran like that, and then like that, and then like that, sort of in a zigzag line, stopping on the northern edge of the desert. But this desert is much harsher than what's around Karawa, so people don't think anybody travels through there.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And nobody really went east of that. So a lot of this is unknown. People are scouting out there because it seems like this border has become fluid in a way that it hasn't in the past.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hmm. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right, so Alesh had said before she had never rode past the canyon, right? She'd never rode that far. Yes, Kenzo.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: What can you tell us of Raven's Hold? Anything you can tell us about it, its history, what we might expect to find there.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Raven's Hold. Raven's Hold is quite interesting, because it was not just a fortress, but it was a holdfast, a place where the few people of the North... So I don't know if you know this about our people's history, Kenzo, but you know, before the Great Upheavals and before the Great War, the North was still not so safe, right? So there was forts and, you know, wars with hobgoblins, wars with other stranger, more deadly creatures. It's a place I'd love to visit sometime.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I've heard... I've never been there. I've heard from travelers, right? So it's near the road. It's near one of the trade routes to Sembara, and so every now and then we'll get people, usually around this time, actually. I wish that I hadn't been out riding and scouting so much, because the festival is always one of the best times to hear stories and lore from travelers. But sorry, I'm... What was your question? I'm getting distracted.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: About Raven's Hold. What can you tell us about Raven's Hold?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Raven's Hold. So not only is it a defensive fortification, but it was also a place where... At least what people say is that there used to be dwarves that lived in those mountains as well. I think many of them have moved southwest to the Yuvanti Mountains because, of course, with the upheavals, the southern part of the central mountain range has become quite dangerous. And Raven's Hold was not just a place to defend Dunmari, but also a place to trade with dwarves.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And the story goes that there are ancient dwarven roads that run hundreds of miles underneath the mountains and that dwarves would travel along these ancient roads south to this as one of the southernmost points of their kingdom and use that as a trading outpost to, you know, exchange grain for ore and things like that with the Dunmari.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Did I know about this?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Do what?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Did I know about that?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, this is quite far to the south of your homeland. You know that there used to be other dwarven kingdoms. So like you're part of the sort of more northern dwarves. There definitely were like southern dwarves and they all left the mountains. So the central mountain chain that runs up the middle of the continent was at one point filled with dwarves. But everything south of Ulrich Monastery basically fled after all the disaster. And the people, your people who live north of there sort of lost contact with the southern dwarves after the war.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: But you would have known there used to be a dwarven kingdom there. And given your history proficiency, you would have known that they traded with the Dunmari. The details about Raven's Hold wouldn't have been part of your study, but...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: But hundreds of miles of underground highways.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You've traveled on dwarven roads that go hundreds of miles underground. This isn't that unusual to you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: But just that they're in this location, I didn't know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That they're in this location, you didn't realize.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Word.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh kind of looks at her companions, and she says, "You know that I could stay here talking history all evening, but friends, we must go if we're to make any distance tonight before it gets dark. I wish you luck on your journey. Stay safe. Travel carefully. And we'll meet back here hopefully in three weeks' time."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You as well and safe travels.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And with that, she rides off. Okay. Anything else you want to do before tomorrow, the festival?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: No. Well, nothing.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Seeker, what do you think about fortifications for the temple? Have you begun thinking of the best plan there? And do you need help?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I'll be right back, guys.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I've surveyed a little bit, but I'll need Tim's help to figure out what is actually possible. So, for instance, my ability to shape the stone relies on it being a little bit loose. And then my ability to, like, actually, like, help the non-magical fortification of it depends on my masonry skills, I guess.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So I would say, given the combination of your masonry skills and your magical ability to shape earth and stone, you don't have a lot of time. You can't build a whole another wall or something like that. But if you spend most of the afternoon, most of the next day, sort of up until the festival on this, you could make something like a secondary wall kind of in front of the temple.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And basically also spend a lot of time reinforcing doors and walls, so that it would be much harder to break something down. Temple's in pretty good shape because not very much of it sticks out of the mesa, right? And so if you can just fortify the part that sticks out of the cliff wall, nobody can get in through the cliff, right?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: There's no back entrance. There's no side entrance.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, none that you're aware of, none that Candrosa's told you about. So I would say, if you want to just make a... Let's see, what would this be? Make an Intelligence check and then add four, which is twice your proficiency bonus, because using shape earth and stone to aid you makes you much better at masonry.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Nice. So wait, I'm going to roll the Intelligence check.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Roll an Intelligence check and then add four to it. So 18.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. So I'll say it takes you most of the next day, and you'll come back to the inn just to clean up for an hour before the festival starts. But you feel pretty comfortable with the job that you've done, and you think that you've definitely made a difference, right? It's gonna be much harder to... Certainly, if somebody comes in and tries to break the main door down or something like that, it's gonna be much more difficult.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: One crucial thing is I've multiple times now used the trick of tripping up a monster by undercutting it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: So I'm gonna make like—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Some pit traps?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Just more like a moat, a dry moat.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay. Yeah, yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: With a wall on the other side of it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. Okay.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Um—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So that's perfect. Yeah, you can do that. That's easy with mold earth and stone because the loose dirt around the base of the temple is quite easy for you to shape.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It also... There's also this, like, make normal terrain into difficult terrain.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: The problem is—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... people will need to be able to get in and out a little bit.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Um—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, I mean, so you can do something like, you know, there's second story windows, right? They can have a rope ladder and come in and out via—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... via something like that. So you could really fortify the front door such that it's really quite difficult to—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I had been—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... get past.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... I had been thinking we had to do this after the festival, but the festival is with different gods, so not this temple.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Right, right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] I was mixed up about that before. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay. So again, anything else? So fortifications, you've sort of dealt with everything else you want to deal with.

blocks.title: Riswynn and the Festival of Rebirth

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so as you are preparing yourself for the festival: there's a ceremony the first night, and then there's a fast and a procession the next day, and then another ceremony and a feast at the end of the festival. But as you're back at Ikram's Caravanserai preparing to go, I assume you're gonna attend the festival.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: At least some of you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's why you're here. Um—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm-hmm. Definitely.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Hold on one sec. I don't know where Kate went, and her character is about to be introduced.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, nice. [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So I need to find her. Are you ready? Oh, okay. So as you're sitting in the inn getting ready for the festival, Ikram comes over to you and says, "Raven's Hold, huh? I know it's maybe not what you were expecting, but a traveler arrived this morning to town who said she's also heading to Raven's Hold. And I said, 'Hey, you should talk to these folks.'" And he waves over, and as you're all sitting here having your meal before the festival starts, you see...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Kate, do you wanna describe your character?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: So you see a dwarf whose red hair is braided in, like, intricate braids. She's wearing armor that's very devotedly maintained, heftily armed with her mace and her shield. She looks ready to maintain a journey of some distance and determined to reach her destination.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And do you guys wanna describe your characters briefly? Somebody.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Delwath is an elf. He's wearing... He is not carrying any weapons. He's wearing a suit of chain mail and has pale silver hair and sort of a copper skin and golden eyes. He looks, I guess, exotic more than anything else. I mean, elves are obviously quite unusual.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: And Kenzo, Kenzo's human, Dunmari, dark hair, very, very fit looking, athletic, but also wearing just kind of loose traveler's outfits, light robe. Apparently has two staffs kind of slung, connected back behind on his chair. Actually, I guess the staff's probably on my horse. Whatever. Anyways, one staff. And yeah.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Wellby is a halfling in studded leather armor with a bow and quiver poking up over his shoulder and a wide-brimmed hat to keep the sun out of his eyes, and boots and clothes that have clearly seen a lot of miles on them.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Seeker is a dwarf with a large, carefully braided red beard, which is either braided in extremely unfashionable style or from the distant, distant northern dwarven peoples. He wears scholarly looking robes and appears a bit frazzled and is currently attempting to pick what looks like sandstone dust out of his eyebrows.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Ikram is the innkeeper. Ikram says, "I guess I'll let you talk, but let me know if you need food or anything, and don't forget the festival. She said Raven's Hold, and I knew somebody had mentioned Raven's Hold to me, and then I thought, 'Oh, I know who it was. I know just the people.'"

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Thanks.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Wonderful.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Excellent introduction.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Traveler, what brings you to Raven's Hold, or why are you headed to Raven's Hold?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: So my name is Riswynn, and I live in the Yuvanti Mountains in the city of Tharn Todor. And I am on a quest for the benefit of my clan. I don't know what you've heard or what your connection is to Raven's Hold, but we dwarves are aware that there are some rumors that dwarvish artifacts are disappearing into the west, and of course we don't approve. And there are dwarves who've mounted a larger quest, a massive push to sort of retrieve and restore things that we had left behind in our exodus from the Central Mountains when we moved down to the Nardith and the Yuvanti.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: And so we Brawn—well, Brawnanvils have a connection to Raven's Hold, and one of our family artifacts is there. And since it's so far to the east, it might be one of the last things collected or even forgotten entirely by the main dwarvish party. So my clan has sent me to recover this artifact of our clan. Though I've heard that there is some troubling violence and unsafety in this region. And so I thought instead of just continuing my quest solo to Raven's Hold, it might be wise to seek some traveling companions.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That is all very fascinating information.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'm Seeker. I come from Highkeep. I'm Seeker of Highkeep. Way far, far to the north of here is my family's holdings. I've come this way south on my own spiritual journey, but fallen in with this band of interesting folks trying to do what we can to protect the peoples of this area.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Did you keep to the mountains on your journey south? Or, like, have you already been to the Raven's Hold area?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I have not been through there, nor have the rest of us. Is that true? No. None of us have been nearby. I'm very interested to learn more about these artifacts, but perhaps we can discuss along the way. I was gifted just recently a book, but I do not know who gave the gift or what the origin is of the book. Does that sound familiar?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: No. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It is a book of runes, the runes of our people.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Runes are very significant to all of us, of course. I only have particular knowledge of a few myself, but I can see that the book would be a treasure. It's impressive that something just landed in your lap.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It's quite a beautiful artifact. I take it out, and I don't open the book itself, but just to show off the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It is, I mean, it's very nice. The cover itself is almost made of stone, like very finely polished granite. And it has, in dwarven runes, [coughs] the title is The Runes of Creation, sort of carved in elaborate inlaid letters with little traces of silver and stuff like that.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I've already learned a great deal from the deep study of this book, which caused me to unfortunately miss a few of the axe beak races, but it was worthwhile.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I'm impressed. It looks very exciting.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] I'd hope to learn more about where it came from, but we'll see what we can find out.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hey, Wellby, look at your messages.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Um...

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: So when are you... Are you staying through the festival and then preparing for your journey? Or what is your reason for going to Raven's Hold and your timeframe?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [festive music] Peak in the music. We had thought to leave after the festival.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It is a—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: ... very dangerous time to be traveling by yourself.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That's certainly the case.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I've heard the rumors. Do you know anything about it firsthand or even secondhand?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I do. I spoke with a halfling from one of the caravans who came down through the pass near Raven's Hold. Left the caravan to explore, made it through the outer wall, but once he got through, was attacked by something magically that appears to have made him go completely insane. He's raving and desperate for raw flesh. That's what brings us there, is to figure out what might have happened and why. He said he heard chanting, too.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Mm.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Riswynn, what else do you know about Raven's Hold? Do you know what dangers or other things we might find there?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Well, because it is my family's ancestral home, my great-great-uncle was able to sketch me a bit of a map. So when I get there, I'm sure I'll be able to orient given my knowledge of dwarvish hold layouts and familiarity with the type of architecture of my people. But I haven't actually been there myself, yeah, since before my—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I, like, grab Wellby, kind of affectionately grab Wellby. This guy loves maps. Loves them.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: [laughs] On your maps, is there a way in underground? Are there ways inside that aren't walking through the field of insanity-making vines?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Hmm. Well, insanity-making vines weren't on the map. [laughs] I may have to take a look from some perspective and sort of orient with the information that I have from years ago when Uncle Eberk lived there.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Very good.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Well, it sounds like we'd all benefit from traveling together.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I definitely don't want to brave whatever beasts have been plaguing the peoples of these areas, including maddening enchantments. That—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Riswynn, if you don't mind me being a bit blunt, but can you fight? Can you... We don't know what we're gonna find there at all, and I think our party's only recently really learned over the past couple of weeks how to defend, how to fight, how to kind of deal with unexpected danger. I say this from a place of agreement that traveling together would be wise, but also we have a very urgent quest and need to make sure that we're focused on that.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Well, I can take care of myself and perhaps some of you, too. I mean, the warhammer comes as naturally to the dwarf as anything else, and with the amount of time that I've spent in devotion to the Bahrâzel, I've got some capabilities for spellcasting that help me out when I'm in a battle situation. So...

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: What kind of spells, if you don't mind me asking?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Divine ones. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I like to make sure that my armor is imbued with some spiritual protection, or sometimes a weapon that I carry. I make sure that I can bring down the powers of my gods in some of my blows, or use other things, other powers to make sure they're secure. You know, I'm not all about violence, but I can handle myself.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: As you're talking, you notice that the inn has started to empty out, and Ikram's sort of looking at you, not quite wanting to lock the door while you're talking. He's like, "Come on, you're gonna miss the festival. It's the biggest night of the year." So as you all walk out—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Absolutely.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... to the festival, there's a huge crowd gathered sort of out on the desert. It's probably essentially everybody who is in Karawa, either because they live there or they're here for the festival itself. And people more than usual are deep in prayer. They're sort of kneeling and swaying and offering words of devotion to Jeevali. You see, traveling from the temple, the Priestess Suma, dressed in these robes of green and gold, comes out carrying—well, I guess walking in front of a number of pallbearers who are carrying on a large wooden, I don't know what you call them, palanquin-type thing, like a platform basically with poles on either side, this thing that looks kind of like a shrine.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It looks almost like a tree constructed out of vines and pieces of wood and little pieces of the desert. It's standing about eight feet tall, and it's this sort of trunk design with a pattern spiraling up it to the top, and then it explodes out into this crown, and these sort of vines twirl around, but it's all dead. It's brown, dry wood. And she carries it out into the desert, and everybody follows and forms a big circle around it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And Suma begins to tell the story of Jeevali and sort of what the festival is about. And she starts by talking about how Jeevali has always protected the Dunmari. And the story, which, Kenzo, you would have heard, but to the rest of you is new, is that when the Dunmari first settled in this land after the First Great Empire, the Drankorian Empire, had been wiped off the face of the world by this magical plague, it was a dry, dead, barren landscape.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And the people who fled here from the south suffered and died from the drought and the hunger and fear. But Jeevali wept for her people, crying tears that poured from the heavens, cleansing the land, purifying the soil, and creating rivers that flowed to the sea. As she cried, though, she put so much of her power and spirit into her tears that she began to fade away, diminished, and was gone. But the land sprung up in richness and life, and the grass grew, and the herds prospered.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And for a year, the people prayed, singing her name every day, calling to her and begging for her to return. That first harvest in the new land was an incredibly bountiful one. The lambs and calves and foals were healthy and productive and survived. And as the winter rains fell gently on the land, the people prayed and chanted her name. And as the new life began to grow in the fertile soil, Jeevali herself appeared as this living tree with a spiral design growing up to the top, the power of the belief of the people summoning her back from the divine essence and restoring her form.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And since then, the Festival of Rebirth has marked this event, the founding of Dunmar, the grace of Jeevali in saving the people, and the miracle of her restoration. And as she comes to the end of this tale, the people chant, and the sort of song goes through the crowds, and she lights the shrine on fire. And every year at the evening of this festival, the people of Karawa burn this old shrine, and then in a procession in the new year—or in the new day—they bring pieces of the desert. They bring seeds and flowers and plants and create them into this shrine shape again. And then hopefully Jeevali will bless it, and it will grow and thrive.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And of course, this year there's this undercurrent of fear running through the crowd, and worry, and uncertainty as everybody here is contemplating leaving in the next day or two, fleeing west into the... Fleeing from what is not entirely clear. But whatever it is, it seems horrifying.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And as the shrine catches on fire, it sort of bursts into flames. And as it's burning, it doesn't just burn normally. Pieces of it kind of drift off, almost like fireworks, floating in all directions, but mostly west. And as these embers drift to the west, a sort of sigh goes through the crowd as Suma says, "Jeevali has blessed us. Jeevali is going west, and we will follow her." And then offers a prayer in her name and a song, and, "In the morning, the day after the festival, we will gather, and we will leave, and Jeevali will be with us in this journey and keep us safe."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And with that, the fires burn down to the ground, the ashes cool, and a gust of wind sort of swirls around the people, and this ash just kind of blows around everywhere and then [exhales] disperses.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And with that, people kind of drift off. Traditionally, people will fast until the feast after the new shrine is blessed in the midday.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And as you rest and then get up in the morning for the procession, people seem, if not cheerful, at least more ready to face what is coming. Some resigned, some fearful, but all with a sort of sense of determination and relief that they can tell themselves they're going with the goddess's favor. And as you watch the procession... So the first thing in the morning, basically, is there's... People have gathered all these, like, pieces of the desert and pieces of flowers and plants and everything that blooms and grows.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And there's a procession where basically everybody in town slowly files past the temple and starts to collaboratively, as a community, rebuild this shrine. So this procession winds through town singing the praises of Jeevali, and it's normally sort of an almost celebratory atmosphere. People dress up in costumes, and they dance and things like that. Of course, it's more solemn this year, but still people seem prepared, right? The procession winds through town, each participant placing a token or a small offering at the site of the burned shrine: desert flowers, a feather, something like that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And as the day stretches into afternoon, the crowd gathers, and this chant begins as people call on Jeevali to inhabit this new shrine. And you watch as, by some trick of the light or by the magic of the gods, all these individual offerings begin to fuse together. And as this is happening, you hear at the edge of the crowd a murmur starts, a sort of discordant note, which quickly becomes a shout, and then a series of screams.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Against the late afternoon sun, you see a column of dust from the north, rising towards the north, near the outskirts of the large camp just north of town. People are starting to now run in from that direction. What do you wanna do?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Run toward that direction.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: [laughs] What do we always do when people are running away from things?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What do you always do?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Running towards the things.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [sighs] So as you charge in that direction, let's see here. You see... Sort of running towards town in the distance. You're running past everybody who's kind of screaming and falling in. And it's... You haven't... It's just still in the distance, this cloud of dust. And you begin to see, sort of emerging from the north of the town, kind of almost exactly the same route, Kenzo, that you took your very first day in Karawa coming down this hill.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: But now, sort of towards the west, towards the outskirts of the camp, you see a group of creatures... Let's see. Where are you all? Oops. Running from the south. A group of creatures running in this direction. Three of them are beasts that look like half human. Hold on. Let me just set you all up. So three of them are beasts that look like [sighs] almost like humanoid hyenas.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They're snarling. You can hear the sort of yips and shouts as you come across this rise and sort of around the tents. There seems to be, like, blood dripping from their faces even at this distance, carrying two swords that they're pulling out as they start to yell and snarl, running in your direction. Behind them are... Oops. Are three creatures that could best be described as snarling, running mouths. They are—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You say snarling, running mouths?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, they are.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They're—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Oh, boy.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They're basically... Yes, they... Enormous teeth, like a mouth the size of a person with rows and rows of jagged teeth and three or four eyes kind of clustered around it, claws sticking off haphazardly in either direction, running on four legs with, like, drool and spittle and little bits of blood flying behind their mouths as they also are sort of snarling and yipping and screaming in hunger and madness, running towards you. And I need everybody to roll initiative.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh my God. How big are the mouth things?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: About the size of a person.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: How far away are they on this map yet or—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Hold on, hold on. Yeah, yeah, let me put them on the map. One sec.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Also, as we're running north, you'll see, just materializing out of nothingness, a sword appears in Delwath's hand.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I think I rolled twice by accident. Sorry.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Remind me. Is the rolling in the Roll20 or the DM—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, yeah, go into D&D Beyond and click on initiative.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Mm-hmm. Does that do something or do I need to hit this Beyond 20 button thing?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I think that... Yep, that did something. Now I just need to get everybody on the combat. For some reason, it only got Delwath on the turn order, but I'll just add—sorry, my map is jumping around. Okay, so Kenzo is... Kenzo, what did you roll? Eight?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I rolled an eight, yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Riswynn is 19.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Delwath is eight. Seeker, what did you roll?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Two. Ah, look at you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And Wellby is 11. Now let me just add these ones.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Did you roll four times, Seeker?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Twice.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, some of those are Intelligence.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, and Investigation.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right. Oh, I don't know why this isn't adding all of them. Sorry about the slight technical issue here. Okay, that's that one. That's that one.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: And that's that one.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, and then so they're running from this direction, and then the, like, snarling mouth creatures are kind of coming through these tents.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, geez.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Is there a way to measure on this map?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Do you know how?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Click on the little circle with a little ruler in it.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Ah. Hmm. Hmm.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Wait, so where are the mouth guys?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I'm trying to get them set up, but it's... Sorry, I didn't have time to set up the map in advance.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They're over there.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hyena dudes have swords?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hyena dudes—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The hyena dudes have swords, yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... have upgraded.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: The fuck?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: They now have swords. The swords are presumably metallic.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, they are, in fact, metallic.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Relevant. And ugh.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so Seeker is up first.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay. I gotta measure my distance here. So Sleep has a range of 90 feet, so actually I can cast it without moving. Is that true? Let me check that again.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yep, I believe that's true.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And so I'm gonna cast the second-level version of Sleep, I think. That make sense?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Wait, is... There's two...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, whoops, sorry.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: There's—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I did that wrong.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: ... is one of these things a hyena?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, one of those is supposed to be a—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... one of the—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You just did the tokens wrong.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I just did the tokens wrong.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: They're all mouth guys.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They're all mouth guys.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay, okay. This is a little bit metagame, but in terms of the levels of Sleep thing, it really has to do with the amount of hit points these things have and how many there are.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, so Sleep, in general, is better on wounded foes. It's a good way to finish off wounded foes, because once you've reduced their hit points a little bit, you can wipe them out. It's a little less effective at taking out fully healthy people, because if you don't roll high enough, nothing happens. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: So I get 7d8 total, so it's as many as—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... if, whatever that is, 7d8.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So the average of 7d8 is, like, 20... It's, like, 30-ish, something like that.

lines.speaker: Seeker

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Speak with Animals. Hmm. It is not actually an animal.

lines.text: Oh, so this wouldn't apply.

lines.speaker: DM

lines.text: Worry about Ander.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Whoa.

lines.text: ... is starting to shake all around him.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Around Kenzo or around?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Around Kenzo. Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Whoa.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I turn back towards you, wondering how you caused a minor seismic event.

lines.speaker: Kenzo

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I sent you a message, Schwartz. [coughing] So is anybody... Are you actually going over to him, Wellby?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, okay. Is anybody going over to Ander? He's starting to come around. Somebody should, but—

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I'm not even sure—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, oh, sorry. That's not... Yeah, you don't get anything from the hyena dude. I thought you were trying to talk to Ander.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah, we should tie up Ander.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Um...

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Also.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I'll go over to him.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I wanted to keep an eye on Kenzo with a crazy guy like Ander in the vicinity, so I stayed where I was, but I didn't wanna approach the unknown halfling, 'cause I know he doesn't recognize me.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: He's seen me before.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yeah. Let's tie him up.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yep. I'll help with that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so as he comes to, he also seems to be sort of acting similar to this other creature. Like, he's sort of snarling and angry, and he's just sort of screaming in frustration almost. Hmm.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Does the hyena show, like...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What's it carrying?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Does it have anything?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Two swords. It has two swords. It's wearing armor. It's not good quality. It's tattered. But it's, you know, like studded leather, right? It's not carrying much else besides weapons and armor. I mean, it has... Food or water? It does have a waterskin. There's a few strips of raw flesh sort of tied around it, but it doesn't seem like it's carrying much in the way of food.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You know, it doesn't seem to have a significant amount of gear. There's a leg of a goat tied in a loop slung over its back that's been partially gnawed on. And it has a few bones, sort of like a crudely constructed necklace-type thing, tied as an amulet or something around its neck.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: What are the bones of?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They're, like, knucklebones of probably not a... Well, make a Medicine check.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: And we're on the north side of town, right? These guys were coming from the north? Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Coming from the north. I mean, they're mammalian, probably bones from some sort of antelope or ungulate or some sort of animal like that. Like, bits of the ankle, bits of the wrist bone. lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: In terms of the body structure, like, which parts are human? Which parts are hyena?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's basically a humanoid, hands normal like a humanoid. But it clearly can run—you saw it running on all fours. Its back legs are much more hyena-like, and then it has basically a hyena-like face and sort of mane stretching back down its neck, and big ears. And teeth, like very, you know, carnivore scavenger teeth. So it's really sort of its torso and arms that are the most humanoid-like.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Freaky. Turn some music up. And Ander and the hyena thing had a similar affect. [sniffs] This was sort of like incoherent bloodlust.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, so it's more sort of anger. It's like, I mean, Ander is sort of yelling almost like in disappointment and anger. He's just kind of—

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Was it more responding towards the maws originally, and now that they're gone, he's chilling out? Or is he, like, now sort of focused on the hyena somehow?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He doesn't seem... Yeah, he was definitely running towards the mouth creatures.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Why? That's weird.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I'll say to everyone: he was saying that he was ready to be eaten, that he wanted to be eaten, as if he was running to them in order to be consumed by them.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Has anybody seen anything like these mouths on legs before? [sniffs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Make an arcana check, Seeker.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Do-do—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And, Delwath, you're proficient in arcana, right?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yep. Eight.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So let's see...

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I read a whole book about mouth creatures.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: [laughs] They're the natural enemy of dentists.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Just part of your undergrad thesis, I thought.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Exactly. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Mouth creatures are an essential part of geology.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs] Yeah, yeah. They're an essential part of geology. So you think about this for a while, and you recall... Right, so you've been interested in sort of the idea of other planes and how that connects to magic for a long time. And so at one point, you studied back, before you even left your home city, in one of the older libraries there. And there was a book called Intrusions From the Darker Planes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And in that book, a lot of it was sort of speculation about the kinds of creatures and sort of evil that can seep through the darker places in the multiverse. And you remember seeing a picture that looked very similar to this, described as being the sort of foot soldiers in the army of the dark lord of hunger.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Appropriate.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'm gonna relay this information, as strange as it sounds.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And it seemed clear from that book that these were extraplanar entities, like they were not from this world, was the description, was the context that you would have read this in.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: But how would they get here? Man.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So you do know that there are some more powerful magics that can summon demons and other creatures like that. So it's definitely possible. It's something you're aware is not out of the realm of possibility, but it requires fairly powerful magics to do.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We should try to regroup and make sure nothing else comes in.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: We kill the hyena thing? Not really telling us anything. We don't want it to get loose.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, yeah. What do you do with the hyena thing?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I mean, does it seem... It doesn't respond to attempts to communicate with it.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: So if we, like, let it free, it's not just gonna run away. [laughs]

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: There's no rehabilitation.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yeah, it's all retributive justice.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] Retributive.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: There's no sense of restorative justice in Karawa.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] Brutal.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: So I think there's no way that it, I mean...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, it doesn't...

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I was more thinking there's no way we could, you know, it wouldn't lead us back to its base or anything like that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It seems too far... You get the sense that if you untie it, it's just gonna attack you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Attack, yeah, that's, yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Keep trying to attack you until you or it are dead.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Can we tell anything, like, looking at that and the other dead creatures, anything about where they might have come from? You know, the difference between, like, the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, let's kill it.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: ... sandy desert to the south versus, like, the, I don't know, the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So at least just from looking around, they probably came from the north.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Can we follow their tracks? We did a good job on the last ones.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yes, we can.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You can. [laughs] Indeed, you can.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We should see if the mouth creatures make distinct tracks and if they came from the same place or—

lines.text: So let's kill this hyena thing. Let somebody go, or all of us go, maybe reassure the town that they didn't, you know, that...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They should flee probably.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Advance your fleeing timetable.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Right.

lines.text: To now. I'll take Ander back to the halfling as well.

lines.text: Okay, so as you start to take him back, Bree and Callie you see sort of running from the distance. And as they see you with him and him walking... And they're quite relieved, extremely relieved to see him alive.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And Callie just kind of looks shocked at you, and, "He just ran off. We heard these things coming and we ran with everybody else as far as we could, and he just turned and ran straight towards them."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: So he was trying to feed himself to one of those, looking at the mouths.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Her face turns white, and she steps back in horror and just holds her arm up: "No, don't... I can't." And she turns her back and is, "Don't tell me what that was. I... lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: She's clearly extremely distraught at this news and the sight of this battle.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Wellby—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And then—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: ... attempts to be comforting, but Wellby is very much, like, not a people person. He's very—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: ... very bad people skills. He's like, "Well, we'll track them back north and attempt either to break the spell or let you know we have them."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So the halflings kind of shuffle off as you hear hoofbeats coming from the east as Havdar rides up, his spear bloodied and a gash across his chest, and he says, "Ooh, thank God. "Two of these attacked on the other side of the hill, and they seemed like they were sneaky."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "They were shooting at people with arrows, and I charged towards them just praying that, as I saw the four of you run off—five of you run off—you would be able to deal with these attackers. lines.text: So by the way, this whole time, everything that's been going on, Kenzo has not moved. Kenzo has just stayed exactly... The earth was shaking for a little while, and he's just not moved, stayed in meditative pose this entire time, just sitting there.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: You do this often? Have you all seen this before?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Well, he is a monk, but we haven't seen this specific thing.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wait, so h—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Check your messages.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Havdar's the guy that just rode up?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We should let you know that in addition to these hyena guys, we just defeated a much stranger group of creatures. They were all mouth, you might say. I don't know if there's any identifiable remains that I can point you to.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's some bits. I mean, the one that Riswynn destroyed with the spell is pretty much scattered to pieces, but—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Sorry.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... the—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs]

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... the other two are still intact enough you can look at their corpses.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And as you are sort of standing here, you can see that the corpses are decaying faster than normal, right? lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's not little bits of flesh scattered around the battlefield. It's just gone.

lines.text: How does Havdar react?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, he... I mean, you can see he wasn't expecting that, and he sort of steels himself a little bit and is acting... You know, he is an arrogant warrior dude. lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hyena.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: ... hyena creatures. "That is unsettling. I am impressed with your prowess in not blanching in the face of a creature with so many teeth. But I have not seen such a thing before."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: They seem to be very dangerous.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Perhaps came from the Blasted Plains. There could be anything out there."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: From my—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Or do you think it came from the north, from Raven's Hold?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: From my—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I guess there could be anything there, either.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... from my studies, as far as I know, this type of creature comes not from this world at all, but from another, from a darker plane. Who knows how they got here? We'd like to try to find out.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "That sounds like a dangerous mission, but..." And now he's looking around, and he turns to Riswynn and says, "I don't believe we've been introduced." Sort of gives a little bow. "Havdar."

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Riswynn.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Are you with them?

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: It seemed prudent, with such things about, to join some other travelers headed in the same direction, so—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You're heading to Raven's Hold.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: I am.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I wish you luck. I must return and supervise the gathering of forces. I suspect that we will be packing and preparing all night. lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: The hyena creatures you encountered, you were able to take them both down, or did they head off in some direction?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, yes, I was able to take them down. Nasty barbed arrows, but nothing that a few quick spear thrusts and a horse charge can't cure.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: One of ours we put magically to sleep. What's its status now?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: We killed it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They killed it.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh. Never mind.

lines.speaker: Riswynn
lines.text: Ours had swords, but we'll keep an eye out for the barbed arrows.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That sounds nasty, too.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, watch your backs. Travel quick, travel quiet, travel carefully. lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We'll just hope those staying here to protect the temple to Shakun have sufficient defenses.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I will say I think you've done a nice job. I was inspecting it this morning.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, thanks.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "The fortifications are, I think, the best we could do in the time, and I will pray for their safety. I'm sure they will pray for their safety as well. With that, I must away." And people are shifting quickly from what normally would have been a sort of celebratory feast at the end of the festival, as the Shrine of Jeevali grows into its sort of fused, divinely imbued form, to a hurried evacuation, gathering in the night what they can.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You know, they're getting on horses and just moving as fast as they can. Many of the people who are here came in for the festival and so are prepared to travel. Many are leaving their homes. But given what's happened this evening, it's... Everybody is in a state of just flat-out preparation to flee.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Kisa and Candrosa come to thank you and wish you off and say, "This does not change our plans. It just advances the timeline, and—"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Sorry, have we gone into town? Because Kenzo's not moved. Kenzo's still—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, people are coming out here.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... okay, okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "This changes nothing. This just means we must flee as quickly as we can." lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Are you gonna stay, Kenzo, just meditating out here through the night?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Is anybody gonna come and say anything to me, or you're just, like, ignoring me?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, yeah, [laughs] that's a good question. Is anybody gonna say anything to you?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Well, I thought, like, Havdar, I don't know if you would've noticed I was just kinda sitting there, or if they were gonna come, and I just have not moved. I'm gonna—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So that's why—Candrosa, when Candrosa comes up, he does sort of look over at you. "Is Kenzo okay?"

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: He was badly injured in the fighting.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Just so you're actually asking if I'm okay? Is anybody talking to me, or is everybody just talking about me after the—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I think we're just talking about you.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Well, I'll come up to Kenzo after Havdar leaves and sit down sort of next to you and just ask, and just look at Kenzo like, "Are you responding to somebody being near you?"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So if you come over and kinda sit down near me, then yeah, then Kenzo kinda stirs a little bit and then... So it's just Delwath?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay. So yeah, Kenzo kind of stirs a little bit and then comes out of his meditation, out of his trance, and he looks at you, but his eyes are, like, bright blue, like, just brilliant blue eyes. And he just kind of looks at you, and he says, "Delwath, is the battle over?"

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Did we win?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yes, you were there.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: So I've been rummaging around in the ruins, trying to extract one of the teeth of the mouth creatures—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: ... but I turn when I hear the voices and see the glowing of the eyes and—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: This is unusual. Your eyes are not normally blue?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, no, they're normally, like, brown eyes, so.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: They're, like, piercing blue eyes, like diamonds, like incredibly bright blue eyes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Now, when you did your Hadouken, was that blue?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Sure. Yeah. It was.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Nice, okay.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: It's the snow cone.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: ... mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: [laughs] A glowing blue ball of force.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, exactly.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Love it. That works.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Totally blue. No, perfect. I love that. Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Mm-hmm. Just kinda stare at your glowing eyes for a second.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Um...

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Say, "Hey, Kenzo, you good?"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I don't know. I don't know. I feel like I've crossed into the void.

lines.text: You took a lot of bites from these guys. I hold up the... Did I find a tooth, Tim?

lines.text: Yeah. You can extract a tooth.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Do you think—

lines.text: I mean, it's black, and it's almost steaming, and it feels slightly warm to the touch.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.text: I throw a waterskin towards Kenzo if he needs some more physical recoveries.

lines.text: Nice.

lines.text: What was that, Kate? Or what was that, Riswynn?

lines.text: I reach a waterskin towards you in case you—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Ah.
